relevant_findings.topic: Exterior trim is LF-based, not SF-based
relevant_findings.finding: All exterior trim components are measured in linear feet (LF). Per PCA P10 one-foot rule, trim with girth < 12 inches is quantified as 1 SF per LF — this compensates for the detailed work difficulty of narrow trim surfaces. The LF measurement is the primary quantity; the one-foot rule is applied inside production rate calibration, not as a UOM conversion in the spec.

This spec covers 8 distinct exterior trim components, each with its own PaintScope key: fascia (PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.FASCIA), rake (PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.TRIM_RAKE), frieze (PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.TRIM_FRIEZE), corner boards (PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.TRIM_CORNER), band boards (PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.TRIM_BAND), window casings (PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.TRIM_WINDOW_CASING), door casings (PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.TRIM_DOOR_CASING), and sills (PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.SILL). All are LF-based.

relevant_findings.topic: Brush is the primary application method for trim
relevant_findings.finding: Brush is the dominant application method for exterior trim. Per Application Methods Doctrine, brush is the precision tool for trim, details, and small areas. Spray is secondary and used for long fascia/frieze runs where masking is economical. Brush production rate for exterior trim: 50-100 SF/hr (general), 40 LF/hr (Trim Systems Doctrine specific). Spray production rate for trim: 100-150 SF/hr including constant repositioning.

relevant_findings.topic: Height/access is the dominant cost modifier for exterior trim
relevant_findings.finding: Fascia, rake, and frieze are ALWAYS elevated work. Height modifiers from Trim Systems Doctrine: 8ft=1.30, 13ft=1.60, 17ft=1.90, 19ft=2.20. These are MORE AGGRESSIVE than the general access modifiers (ladder=1.35, scaffold=1.60) because trim work requires fine brush detail at height, not just broad spray application. The Trim Systems Doctrine height modifiers take precedence for trim-specific tasks.

relevant_findings.topic: Three substrate materials with different primer requirements
relevant_findings.finding: Exterior trim encompasses three substrate materials: (1) Traditional wood — requires acrylic latex primer for tannin blocking and moisture management; (2) Cellular PVC (AZEK, VERSATEX) — requires bonding primer to grip the dense, non-porous surface; glossy PVC must be scuff-sanded with 220-grit first; (3) Composite/engineered wood (LP SmartSide) — requires mandatory edge sealing on all field-cut edges with primer + 100% acrylic latex per warranty.

relevant_findings.topic: LRV constraint for PVC trim — solar-reflective coatings required below LRV 55
relevant_findings.finding: Dark colors (LRV < 55) on cellular PVC trim cause excessive heat absorption leading to warping, buckling, and voided warranties. Standard paint on PVC trim MUST have LRV 55+ unless solar-reflective coatings (VinylSafe, Colors for Vinyl) are specified. This is a HARD STOP — if color LRV < 55 and substrate is PVC, spec must require solar-reflective coating or reject the color.

relevant_findings.topic: Caulking is integral to trim painting — sequenced AFTER primer
relevant_findings.finding: Trim-to-trim joints, corner joints, and casing joints must be caulked AFTER primer application. Caulk adheres better to primed surfaces than bare substrates, and priming first seals and stabilizes the wood/PVC/composite edges before caulk is applied. This caulking is integral to the trim painting scope, distinct from SF_CAULK_EXT_v1 which covers standalone expansion joints and specialty sealant work. NOTE: Trim-to-siding joint caulking may also be scoped under the siding spec — the estimation engine must deduplicate at project assembly to prevent double-counting caulk labor at the trim-siding junction. Sealant for PVC: solvent-based polymer (NPC Solar Seal #900, OSI Quad) or polyurethane — NEVER silicone (lacks PVC compatibility). Sealant for wood: same options. Caulking rate: 75-150 LF/hr depending on joint complexity.

relevant_findings.topic: Sheen is a project-level selection — no locked-in default for exterior trim
relevant_findings.finding: There is no locked-in default sheen for exterior trim. Sheen is a project-level color/sheen configuration decision. Valid sheens for exterior trim are satin, semi-gloss, and gloss. Satin is the most common selection for exterior trim in practice. The spec must not hardcode a sheen default — it is always a user selection.
relevant_findings.source: Eric correction — Exterior_Color_Sheen_Configuration_Doctrine.md §3 lists recommendations but does not mandate defaults

relevant_findings.finding: Built-up trim profiles (stacked crown systems, multi-piece cornice assemblies) add +30% to +60% labor increase over standard flat trim profiles. This complexity modifier applies to production rates for both brush and spray application. Crown profiles have inside corners, shadow lines, and multiple planes that require additional brush time and masking.

relevant_findings.topic: Top-down painting sequence for exterior trim
relevant_findings.finding: Correct sequencing per doctrine is top-down: (1) fascia, soffits, eaves first; (2) siding/stucco walls; (3) trim accents, doors, casings. This means fascia/rake/frieze are painted BEFORE siding, while window/door casings and corner boards may be painted before or after siding depending on crew strategy (trim-first vs body-first).

Exterior trim uses QT3-QT5 range. QT3: standard 2-coat with clean edges. QT4: premium materials, light sand between coats, raking light inspection. QT5: supreme — spray + hand-sand between coats, highest scrutiny. QT2 is NOT applicable to exterior trim. Note: exterior trim is NOT fine-finish work like interior millwork — it is standard exterior grade work, but the visible architectural role justifies QT3 minimum.
relevant_findings.source: Exterior_Application_Methods_Doctrine.md Part B §7; Exterior_Trim_Systems_Doctrine.md §7; Eric correction

relevant_findings.topic: Primer selection is substrate-driven for exterior trim
relevant_findings.finding: Primer type is determined by substrate material: Wood = acrylic latex primer (100% acrylic), with alkyd spot-prime for tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood) knots. PVC = bonding primer (grips dense non-porous surface without sanding requirement on most glossy surfaces). Composite/engineered wood = 100% acrylic latex primer with mandatory edge seal on field-cut edges.

relevant_findings.topic: PVC trim requires special surface prep
relevant_findings.finding: Cellular PVC trim (AZEK, VERSATEX) requires: (1) scuff-sand glossy surfaces with 220-grit; (2) wipe cut edges with acetone or denatured alcohol to seal open cells and remove static charge; (3) bonding primer for adhesion. Never use silicone sealant on PVC. The thermal expansion coefficient of PVC is high — flexible coatings (100% acrylic latex or acrylic-urethane blends) are required to avoid cracking.

relevant_findings.topic: Sill is a distinct component with special coating needs
relevant_findings.finding: Exterior window sills receive direct weather exposure (rain, snow, UV) and are horizontal — making them the most vulnerable trim component. Sills often receive a distinct high-durability coating (porch and floor enamel, or heavy-duty trim coat) due to exposure. Per PaintScope catalog, sills have their own key (PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.SILL) separate from window casings.

The 'think like a water drop' protocol defines locations that must NEVER be caulked: window weep holes, bottom overlap of siding boards, metal-to-wood flashing transitions, and bottoms of overlapping trim boards. Caulking these locations traps water and accelerates rot. Only seal: corner joints, trim-to-siding gaps, door casing joints, and wood window perimeters.

substrate_analysis.description: Traditional wood trim — cedar, pine, fir, redwood, poplar. Porous, hygroscopic, workable.
substrate_analysis.key_properties: Requires paint for rot prevention. Subject to tannin bleed from cedar/redwood. Moisture cycling causes movement. Miter joints open across grain.
substrate_analysis.prep_requirements: Sand to remove mill glaze (80-120 grit). Spot-prime knots with alkyd/shellac on tannin-rich species. After prime: caulk all trim joints on primed surfaces.
substrate_analysis.primer_type: 100% acrylic latex exterior primer. Alkyd spot-prime for knots on cedar/redwood/fir.

substrate_analysis.description: Cellular PVC trim — AZEK, VERSATEX. Impervious to moisture, rot, and insects. High thermal expansion coefficient.
substrate_analysis.key_properties: Non-porous dense surface. Painting recommended to seal edges and prevent dirt accumulation. Extremely high thermal expansion — requires flexible coatings. Dark colors cause heat absorption leading to warping.
substrate_analysis.prep_requirements: Scuff-sand glossy surfaces with 220-grit. Wipe cut edges with acetone or denatured alcohol to seal open cells and remove static charge.
substrate_analysis.primer_type: Bonding primer — grips slick non-porous surface. No sanding required on most glossy surfaces when using bonding primer.
substrate_analysis.recoat_interval: As needed — PVC does not degrade from lack of coating

substrate_analysis.description: Engineered wood composite trim — LP SmartSide TrimBoard. Wood strands + zinc borate + resins. Superior dimensional stability.
substrate_analysis.key_properties: Requires mandatory edge sealing on all field-cut edges per warranty. Factory-primed. Better dimensional stability than solid wood.
substrate_analysis.prep_requirements: Seal ALL field-cut edges with primer + 100% acrylic latex paint (warranty requirement). Light sand factory primer for adhesion profile.
substrate_analysis.primer_type: 100% acrylic latex exterior primer. Edge seal with same.

failure_modes.name: Rot and decay
failure_modes.description: High porosity combined with moisture cycling leads to wood rot. Improper caulking traps water behind trim. Miter joints open across grain, creating moisture entry points.
failure_modes.prevention: Full prime coat to seal wood. Caulk joints properly (butt joints preferred). Back-prime concealed surfaces. Do not caulk weep holes or bottom overlaps.
failure_modes.detection: Soft, spongy wood. Dark discoloration. Paint film lifting from substrate.

failure_modes.name: Thermal distortion on PVC
failure_modes.description: Extreme temperature swings or low-LRV dark paint without solar-reflective technology causes PVC to warp, buckle, or permanently deform.
failure_modes.prevention: HARD STOP: LRV < 55 on PVC requires solar-reflective coatings (VinylSafe, Colors for Vinyl). Never use standard dark paint on PVC.
failure_modes.detection: Board warping, buckling, bowing. Gap opening at joints.

failure_modes.name: Edge swelling on composite
failure_modes.description: Failure to prime/paint field-machined or cut edges before installation allows moisture absorption into exposed wood fiber composite, causing edge swelling that ruptures paint film.
failure_modes.prevention: Seal ALL field-cut edges with primer + 100% acrylic latex before installation. Non-negotiable warranty requirement.
failure_modes.detection: Swollen board edges. Paint bubbling at cut ends. Board expansion at joints.

failure_modes.name: Adhesion failure from surface contamination
failure_modes.description: Painting over dirty, chalky, or glossy surfaces without proper prep causes coating to peel or flake. Particularly common on glossy PVC where bonding primer is skipped.
failure_modes.prevention: Clean all surfaces before coating. Scuff-sand glossy PVC with 220-grit. Use bonding primer on PVC. Remove all chalk residue from weathered surfaces.
failure_modes.detection: Paint peeling in sheets. Tape pull test fails. Coating scrapes off easily.

failure_modes.name: Silicone sealant failure on PVC
failure_modes.description: Silicone sealant lacks compatibility with cellular PVC substrates. Silicone will fail at the bond line, allowing water intrusion at joints. Additionally, silicone is not paintable.
failure_modes.prevention: Use solvent-based polymer (NPC Solar Seal #900, OSI Quad) or polyurethane sealant on PVC. NEVER silicone.
failure_modes.detection: Sealant pulling away from PVC at joint edges. Gap opening at caulked joints.

failure_modes.name: Caulk cracking from premature painting
failure_modes.description: Painting over uncured caulk. Caulk beads are ~40 mils thick vs paint at 1-3 mils. Uncured caulk shrinks as it cures, cracking the paint film.
failure_modes.prevention: Allow full cure per sealant type: acrylic latex can be painted after skinning; polyurethane requires 3-7 day cure before painting.
failure_modes.detection: Cracked paint film over caulk joints. Caulk bead showing through cracked paint.

failure_modes.name: Tannin bleed through primer
failure_modes.description: Cedar, redwood, and Douglas fir knots bleed tannins through standard acrylic primer, causing brown/yellow staining on the finish coat.
failure_modes.prevention: Spot-prime visible knots with alkyd or shellac-based primer before applying acrylic primer over remaining surface. Severe tannin staining may require two coats of acrylic primer.
failure_modes.detection: Brown or yellow-brown staining on white or light-colored finish coat, concentrated at knots and grain.

primer_systems.name: 100% Acrylic Latex Exterior Primer
primer_systems.description: Standard exterior primer for wood and composite trim. Remains flexible long-term, resists cracking, peeling, blistering.
primer_systems.notes: Primary primer for wood and composite. Easy application, soap/water cleanup.

primer_systems.name: Bonding Primer
primer_systems.description: Grips dense, non-porous PVC surfaces. Slightly flexible — provides mechanical tooth for topcoat. No sanding required on most glossy surfaces.
primer_systems.recoat_time: Within 1 week (bonding primer dries like peanut brittle if left too long)
primer_systems.notes: MANDATORY for PVC trim. Must not leave exposed for extended periods — loses flexibility.

primer_systems.name: Alkyd/Shellac Spot Primer
primer_systems.description: Spot-applied to visible wood knots on tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood, fir) before full acrylic primer coat. Superior tannin stain blocking.
primer_systems.notes: Used for knot spot-priming only, not full surface. Alkyd tannin-rich wood primers extend to 3-5 days for full cure on severe bleed.

topcoat_systems.name: 100% Acrylic Latex Exterior Trim Paint
topcoat_systems.description: Standard exterior trim finish. Superior UV resistance and flexibility for thermal and moisture movement. Sheen is a project-level selection (satin, semi-gloss, or gloss).
topcoat_systems.notes: No locked-in default sheen. QT3: mid-grade 100% acrylic. QT4: premium (SW Emerald, BM Aura).

topcoat_systems.name: Acrylic-Urethane Blend Exterior Trim Paint
topcoat_systems.description: Premium waterborne enamel with urethane additive for enhanced hardness and scratch resistance.
topcoat_systems.notes: Recommended for QT4-QT5 trim where maximum hardness is required. Sheen is project-level selection.

topcoat_systems.name: Solar-Reflective Exterior Trim Paint
topcoat_systems.description: IR-reflective coating with Complex Inorganic Color Pigments (CICPs). Allows dark visual colors (LRV < 55) on PVC trim without thermal distortion risk.
topcoat_systems.notes: REQUIRED when substrate = PVC AND color LRV < 55. VinylSafe technology enables dark colors safely. Sheen is project-level selection.

coating_systems.coat_system_summary: 1 prime coat + 2 finish coats at all quality tiers. Primer type is substrate-driven. Topcoat quality is tier-driven.

production_rates.pca_p10_note: All trim with girth < 12 inches is quantified as 1 SF per LF per PCA P10 one-foot rule. Production rates below are calibrated per LF and already account for this conversion internally.

brush_trim_general.notes: Brush application, standard flat trim profile at ground level. 40 LF/hr is the doctrine anchor rate.

brush_fascia.notes: Fascia is always elevated. Rate includes cutting in at roofline edge. Height modifier applied separately.

brush_rake.notes: Rake is inclined and elevated. Awkward angle reduces production. Height modifier applied separately.

brush_frieze.notes: Frieze at eave junction. Often straight horizontal run. Height modifier applied separately.

brush_corner_boards.notes: Corner boards are vertical — easier access than fascia but require two faces per board (inside/outside corner).

brush_window_casing.notes: Window casings require precision at glass edge and siding transition. Rate per LF of casing perimeter.

brush_door_casing.notes: Door casings similar to window but typically larger profile. Rate per LF of casing perimeter.

brush_sill.notes: Sills require careful application on horizontal exposed surface. Often requires additional coat due to exposure.

brush_band_board.notes: Band boards are horizontal runs between floors. Similar to frieze in accessibility.

spray_trim_general.notes: Airless spray on trim, constant repositioning. Uses 211-313 tip codes with waterborne enamels. Only practical for long continuous runs (fascia, frieze, band board).

prime_brush_trim.notes: Primer application by brush on trim. Faster than finish because less precision required.

caulk_trim_joints.notes: Caulking trim-to-siding joints. Simple bead: 100-150 LF/hr. With backer rod: 75-100 LF/hr.

prep_sand_pvc.notes: Scuff-sand glossy PVC with 220-grit + acetone wipe on cut edges.

prep_sand_wood.notes: Sand wood trim to remove mill glaze (80-120 grit). Orbital or hand sand.

knot_spot_prime.notes: Brush alkyd/shellac on visible knots. Cedar/redwood/fir only.

edge_seal_composite.notes: Brush primer/sealant on field-cut edges of composite trim.

condition_drivers.impact: Drives primer selection, prep sequence, and coat count. SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD requires full prime. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD skips prime module.
condition_drivers.notes: NC trim is either bare wood/PVC/composite (dominant) or field-primed (prime already applied in a separate mobilization). Substrate state interacts with substrate_material to determine exact primer product.

condition_drivers.impact: Drives primer type (acrylic for wood, bonding for PVC, acrylic + edge seal for composite), prep protocol (sand wood vs scuff-sand PVC), and sealant compatibility (never silicone on PVC).
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION. A single project may have mixed materials (wood fascia + PVC corner boards). Each trim item in PaintScope carries its own material attribute.

condition_drivers.impact: QT3: standard 2-coat, clean edges. QT4: premium materials, light sand between coats, raking light inspection. QT5: spray + hand-sand between coats, highest scrutiny. QT2 is NOT valid for exterior trim.
condition_drivers.notes: Per Application Methods Doctrine, QT5 for trim means spray + hand-sand between coats.

condition_drivers.impact: Brush is primary for trim (precision, detail). Spray viable for long fascia/frieze/band board runs. Spray requires masking of adjacent surfaces. Brush production: 35-45 LF/hr. Spray: 100-150 SF/hr.
condition_drivers.notes: Unlike siding where spray is primary, trim defaults to brush. Spray is secondary and only practical where masking is economical.

condition_drivers.impact: Sheen affects finish appearance and durability. No locked-in default — sheen is a project-level selection. Gloss highlights surface defects and requires better prep.
condition_drivers.notes: Sheen is always a user/project selection. No default is hardcoded.

condition_drivers.impact: Built-up trim profiles (stacked crown, multi-piece cornice) add +30% to +60% labor. Flat trim profiles are the baseline.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a MODIFIER, not a configuration dimension. Does not change workflow — only multiplies production time.

config_dimensions.description: Expected outcome standard for trim finish
config_dimensions.notes: QT2 not valid for exterior trim. QT5 adds hand-sand between coats.

config_dimensions.description: Physical material of the trim substrate
config_dimensions.notes: Drives primer selection, prep protocol, and sealant compatibility. A project may have mixed materials.
Brush is default for trim (precision, detail). Spray only for long continuous runs where masking is economical.

config_dimensions.description: Finish sheen level — project-level selection, no locked-in default
config_dimensions.notes: No locked-in default. Sheen is always a project-level user selection. Do not hardcode a sheen default in the spec.

config_dimensions.description: Starting condition of the trim substrate coating system
config_dimensions.notes: NC trim is primarily bare. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD applies when prime was completed in a prior mobilization.

modifier_catalog.name: Trim height modifier — above 8 ft (2nd story)
modifier_catalog.application: All tasks on fascia, rake, frieze, and upper-story corner/band boards
modifier_catalog.notes: More aggressive than general access modifier because trim requires fine brush detail at height.

modifier_catalog.name: Trim height modifier — above 13 ft
modifier_catalog.application: All tasks on elevated trim above 13 ft

modifier_catalog.name: Trim height modifier — above 17 ft (3rd story)
modifier_catalog.application: All tasks on elevated trim above 17 ft

modifier_catalog.name: Trim height modifier — above 19 ft
modifier_catalog.application: All tasks on elevated trim above 19 ft

modifier_catalog.name: Built-up/crown profile complexity modifier
modifier_catalog.application: Production rate multiplier for built-up trim profiles (stacked crown, multi-piece cornice)
modifier_catalog.notes: Applied to brush and spray rates for complex profiles.

quality_differences.description: Standard residential trim. Full prep and prime per substrate. Two finish coats with mid-grade 100% acrylic (sheen per project selection). Clean cut-in at siding/glass transitions. Caulk all trim joints after prime. Standard inspection at arm's length.

Premium trim finish. Full prep and prime per substrate. Two finish coats with premium materials (SW Emerald Urethane Trim Enamel, BM Aura Grand Entrance, or equivalent acrylic-urethane). Light sand between coats on visible areas. Raking light inspection before second coat. Crisp trim-to-siding lines.
quality_differences.typical_use: High-end residential, showcase homes, curb-appeal priority.

quality_differences.description: Supreme trim finish. Full prep and prime. Spray application preferred for smoothest finish. Hand-sand between coats. Premium acrylic-urethane topcoat. Raking light inspection at each stage.
quality_differences.typical_use: Luxury custom homes, historic restoration, architect-specified trim.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to light_mask when working at height with ladders (drip zone expands)
zones.notes: Ground-level landscape protection below trim work areas. Drop cloths at building perimeter.
Walkways below trim work area. Drop cloth runners.
Window glass adjacent to window casing trim being painted. Masking film or tape to protect glass from brush drips.
Door glass adjacent to door casing trim. Masking film where needed.
Exterior light fixtures mounted on or near trim. Bag or tape over fixture.
When spraying trim, siding adjacent to trim must be masked. Only relevant for spray application method. Brush application has minimal overspray.

protection_zones_analysis.cross_spec_protection_note: When painting window/door casings, this spec IS responsible for adjacent glass masking because the glass is directly adjacent to the casing being painted. This is different from siding spec where window/door protection is delegated to window/door specs. The casing-to-glass edge is THIS spec's cut-in responsibility.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Trim terminates at siding. Cut-in required at trim-to-siding junction. This spec cuts into siding — siding spec does not cut into trim. Caulk joint at this junction AFTER prime (caulk adheres to primed surfaces). Deduplication note: siding spec may also scope this joint — engine must deduplicate.
Fascia and frieze are adjacent to soffit. Cut-in at fascia-soffit junction. Often different colors (trim color vs soffit color).
Window casing trim abuts window glass. Precision cut-in at glass edge. Glass masking is this spec's responsibility.
Door casing adjacent to exterior door slab. Door slab painting is a separate spec. No cut-in — door meets casing with a natural reveal.
Corner boards and band boards may terminate at foundation. No painting responsibility — drop cloth protection only.

adjacency_analysis.key_finding: Unlike siding which has NO edge work, trim has SIGNIFICANT edge work. Trim cuts into siding, soffit, and glass — it is the precision element. The trim spec owns the cut-in at every trim-to-adjacent junction.

affected_conditions.notes: Exterior trim uses the trim-specific height modifiers from Trim Systems Doctrine (8ft=1.30, 13ft=1.60, 17ft=1.90, 19ft=2.20) rather than the general access modifiers. These are more granular and more aggressive because fine brush detail at height is slower than broad spray work at height.

excluded_conditions.rationale: Environmental conditions are NOT estimatable at bid time. Per wood siding and fiber cement sibling spec corrections (RC-003). Wind, temperature, dew point, and sun exposure belong in SOP procedure notes only.

excluded.reason: Varies by time of day, sun angle, season. Not estimatable.
Varies by elevation. Professional painters follow the shade.

exterior_substrate_states.description: New, uncoated wood trim. May have mill glaze requiring sanding. Primary NC state for wood trim.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Sand 80-120 grit to remove mill glaze. Spot-prime knots with alkyd/shellac on tannin-rich species. After prime: caulk all trim-to-trim joints.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: 100% acrylic latex exterior primer. Alkyd spot-prime for knots on cedar/redwood/fir.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Dominant NC state for wood trim. Mill glaze on new lumber prevents primer adhesion — must be sanded off.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Trim with field-applied exterior primer — ready for topcoat.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Light dust-off. Touch-up any damaged primer spots. Minimal prep — surface is paint-ready.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Occurs when prime and finish are split across mobilizations. Direct topcoat application.

exterior_access_type_analysis.treatment: Trim uses its own height modifier tiers from Exterior_Trim_Systems_Doctrine, which are more granular and aggressive than general access modifiers.

scenarios.notes: Trim at ground level (window/door casings on first floor, lower corner boards). Baseline rate.
Second-story trim. Fascia, rake, frieze on 1-story home. Ladder access.
Two-story fascia, gable peaks. Scaffold or tall ladder.
Extreme height. Scaffold or lift required. Production drops to less than half baseline.

exterior_environmental_constraints.note: Environmental constraints documented for SOP reference only. EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers per sibling spec corrections.

sop_reference_only.go_threshold: < 10 mph for spray; brush at any wind

sop_reference_only.note: PVC on south elevation in full sun can exceed 85°F easily — schedule shaded elevations first.

sop_reference_only.rule: Surface temp must be >= 5°F above dew point
Wood trim: < 15% MC before priming. PVC: not a factor (impervious).

valid_input_states.rationale: NC trim is either bare (wood/PVC/composite — primary state) or field-primed (primer applied in prior mobilization). Bare state applies regardless of substrate material — PVC and composite are both 'bare' in the sense that they have no field coating applied. The substrate_material dimension determines which primer system is used.

output_state.rationale: Output state is the painted finish. Actual sheen (satin, semi-gloss, gloss) varies by project-level sheen selection. No default.

adjacent_state_protection_analysis.rationale: If siding is already painted, light masking at trim-siding junction during brush application. If siding is unfinished, no protection needed — it will be painted after trim. Spray application on trim with finished siding: heavy_mask.
Soffit is typically painted before trim (top-down). If already finished, light masking at fascia-soffit junction.
Glass is always a protection target regardless of state. Masking film or tape at glass edge when painting casings.

this_spec_handles: Painting all 8 trim component types (fascia, rake, frieze, corner, band, window casing, door casing, sill)
Caulking trim-to-trim joints and casing joints after prime (trim-to-siding joint caulking may overlap with siding spec — engine deduplicates)
Primer application on all trim substrates (wood, PVC, composite)
Glass masking adjacent to window and door casings being painted
Knot spot-priming on tannin-rich wood species
Edge sealing on composite (LP SmartSide) field-cut edges

other_specs_handle.SF_SIDING_*: Siding field painting. Siding terminates at trim — no cut-in from siding into trim.
other_specs_handle.SF_SOFFIT_EXT_NC_v1: Soffit field painting. Soffit meets fascia/frieze — soffit spec handles soffit side of junction.
other_specs_handle.SF_DOOR_EXT_NC_v1: Exterior door slab painting. Door casing is this spec; door slab is door spec.
other_specs_handle.SF_WINDOW_EXT_NC_v1: Exterior window sash/frame painting. Window casing is this spec; window sash/frame is window spec.
other_specs_handle.SF_CAULK_EXT_v1: Standalone caulking scope — expansion joints, specialty sealant work, large-scale joint remediation. NOT the simple trim-to-siding caulking that is integral to this spec's prep.
other_specs_handle.SF_GUTTER_EXT_NC_v1: Gutter and downspout painting. Gutters mount to fascia but are separate scope.

notes_for_materials_manager: Primer selection is substrate-driven: wood = 100% acrylic latex exterior primer; PVC = bonding primer; composite = 100% acrylic latex + edge sealant.

Topcoat selection is quality-tier-driven: QT3 = mid-grade 100% acrylic; QT4 = premium acrylic-urethane (SW Emerald Urethane Trim Enamel or equivalent); QT5 = same as QT4. Sheen is always a project-level selection (satin, semi-gloss, or gloss).
HARD STOP: PVC substrate + color LRV < 55 = MUST use solar-reflective coating (VinylSafe technology). Standard paint voids warranty and causes thermal distortion.
Sealant for PVC trim joints: solvent-based polymer (NPC Solar Seal #900, OSI Quad) or polyurethane. NEVER silicone on PVC.
Sealant for wood/composite trim joints: polyurethane or siliconized acrylic. Polyurethane requires 3-7 day cure before painting.
Material waste is handled per product at the general level, not per substrate or per spec.
Transfer efficiency: brush = 95-99% (negligible waste); spray = 40-70% (significant waste). Factor spray waste for fascia/frieze runs.
Alkyd/shellac spot primer needed for knot treatment on cedar, redwood, and fir trim.
notes_for_sop_librarian: Module structure: setup → protect → prep (sand, spot-prime knots) → prime → caulk (on primed surfaces) → apply coat 1 → interstage (QT4/QT5 sand) → apply coat 2 → cleanup → teardown.

Caulking happens AFTER primer, not before. Caulk adheres better to primed surfaces and priming first seals/stabilizes substrate edges. Caulk all trim-to-trim joints and casing joints on primed surfaces.
Never caulk: window weep holes, bottom overlap of siding boards, metal-to-wood flashing transitions, bottoms of overlapping trim boards.
PVC prep module: scuff-sand 220-grit + acetone wipe on cut edges. Different from wood prep (80-120 grit sand for mill glaze).
Composite prep module: edge seal ALL field-cut edges with primer/sealant BEFORE prime coat. Warranty requirement.
Knot spot-prime: cedar/redwood/fir knots with alkyd or shellac BEFORE full acrylic primer coat.
QT4: light sand between finish coats. QT5: hand-sand between finish coats with raking light inspection at each stage.
QT5 application: spray preferred for smoothest finish. Spray + hand-sand between coats.
Sill treatment: consider additional coat or high-durability coating due to extreme horizontal weather exposure.
Sequencing: follow top-down — fascia/rake/frieze first, then casings and corner boards. Match whole-house sequence (high details first, then body, then accents).
Polyurethane caulk cure: minimum 3-day cure before primer/paint. Acrylic latex caulk: paintable after skinning.
notes_for_estimation_engineer: This spec is LF-based with 8 distinct paintable items, each with its own PaintScope key. Do not aggregate all trim into a single quantity.
Production rates vary by component. Fascia/frieze/band: 30-40 LF/hr brush. Rake: 25-35 LF/hr (inclined). Corner: 35-45 LF/hr. Casings: 30-40 LF/hr. Sill: 25-35 LF/hr.
Height modifiers use the trim-specific tiers: 8ft=1.30, 13ft=1.60, 17ft=1.90, 19ft=2.20. These are MORE AGGRESSIVE than general exterior access modifiers.
Height modifier applies per-component based on installed elevation. Fascia is always elevated. Window casings on first floor may be at ground level. Corner boards span multiple height zones.
Complexity modifier for built-up profiles: 1.30-1.60x on production rate. Applied to affected components only (typically fascia/frieze with crown builds).
Coat system: 1 prime + 2 finish coats at all QTs. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD skips prime. QT4/QT5 add interstage sand.
Caulking labor: estimate as separate line item within prep module. 75-120 LF/hr. Not embedded in painting production rate.
Material waste is handled per product at the general level, not per spec.
Environmental conditions (wind, dew point, sun, temp) are EXCLUDED from estimation — SOP/process concerns only. Per sibling spec corrections.
Masking labor for spray trim: estimate as separate line item. Masking-to-spray ratio: 3:1 to 4:1.
Each item may have a different height modifier. Estimate per-item, not as a single aggregated trim quantity.

key_decisions.decision: Combined (full phase_scope). Prime and finish phases have unique task keys within the single spec.
key_decisions.rationale: NC exterior trim is typically a single mobilization — same crew primes and paints. Each phase has its own task IDs and module IDs. Matches siding sibling spec pattern.

key_decisions.decision: 8 distinct paintable items, each with its own PS_EXT_EDGE_LF key. Tasks run per-item.
key_decisions.rationale: Each trim component has different production rates, different typical height, and may have different substrate material. Aggregating all trim into one quantity loses this critical granularity. Per PaintScope_Exterior_Key_Catalog.

key_decisions.decision: QT2 is NOT valid for exterior trim. Minimum QT3.
key_decisions.rationale: Exterior trim is standard exterior grade work but its visible role warrants QT3 minimum. QT2 is appropriate for rental/budget siding field but not for trim work. Per Application_Methods_Doctrine Part B §7.

key_decisions.decision: Include substrate_material dimension: wood, pvc, composite.
key_decisions.rationale: Substrate material drives fundamentally different primer systems, prep protocols, and sealant requirements. Not a modifier — it changes the task workflow.

key_decisions.topic: Trim-specific height modifiers vs general access modifiers
key_decisions.decision: Use Exterior_Trim_Systems_Doctrine height modifiers (8ft/13ft/17ft/19ft tiers) instead of general access_type modifiers.
key_decisions.rationale: Trim doctrine height modifiers are specifically calibrated for brush work at height on narrow components. They are more granular (4 tiers vs 3) and more aggressive at the same heights because trim brush work is harder at elevation than broad spray work on siding.

key_decisions.topic: Caulking scope — integral to trim spec, sequenced after prime
key_decisions.decision: Trim joint caulking is INTEGRAL to this spec, sequenced AFTER primer (not before). Not delegated to SF_CAULK_EXT_v1.
key_decisions.rationale: Caulking trim joints is part of the trim painting workflow. Caulk is applied AFTER primer because: (1) caulk adheres better to primed surfaces than bare substrates; (2) priming first seals and stabilizes the wood/PVC/composite edges. SF_CAULK_EXT_v1 covers standalone expansion joints and specialty sealant scopes. NOTE: Trim-to-siding joint caulking may also be scoped under the siding spec — estimation engine must deduplicate at project assembly.

key_decisions.topic: Glass masking ownership for casing painting
key_decisions.decision: This spec IS responsible for window/door glass masking when painting casings.
key_decisions.rationale: Unlike siding where window/door protection is delegated to other specs, the casing-to-glass edge is this spec's direct cut-in responsibility. Glass must be masked to paint the casing cleanly.

key_decisions.decision: Brush is default. Spray is secondary option for long continuous runs only.
key_decisions.rationale: Trim is precision work. Brush provides highest control, best adhesion (mechanical working), and minimal waste. Spray requires extensive masking that negates speed advantage on short runs. Spray only practical for fascia/frieze/band board long runs.

key_decisions.decision: 1 prime + 2 finish coats at all quality tiers.
key_decisions.rationale: Exterior coating durability depends on proper film build from 2 coats. QT4/QT5 add interstage sanding, not additional coats.

key_decisions.topic: NC substrate states limited to bare and field-primed
key_decisions.decision: Only SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD and SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD as valid input states.
key_decisions.rationale: This is an NC spec. NC trim is either bare (new installation) or field-primed (prime mobilization already completed). Repaint states (sound paint, chalking, peeling) would require a separate repaint spec with different prep modules. Bare state applies to all three substrate materials — the material dimension determines primer selection.

key_decisions.decision: Wind, temperature, dew point, sun exposure EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers.
key_decisions.rationale: Per sibling spec corrections (RC-003 from wood siding, RC-007 from fiber cement). Environmental conditions are unpredictable at bid time. SOP reference only.

assumptions.value: New construction exterior trim painting — fascia, rake, frieze, corner boards, band boards, window casings, door casings, sills. All LF-based.
assumptions.note: Soffit is NOT included (separate spec). Gutters/downspouts are NOT included (separate spec). Door slab and window sash/frame are NOT included (separate specs).

assumptions.value: NC-only: SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD and SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD. Repaint excluded.
assumptions.note: Bare state applies to all three substrate materials. Material dimension determines primer, not state.

assumptions.value: QT2 not valid for exterior trim
assumptions.note: Exterior trim is standard exterior grade work but its visible architectural role justifies minimum QT3.

assumptions.value: Brush is default application method for trim
assumptions.note: Spray is secondary — only for long continuous runs.

uncertainties.detail: Production rates for PVC trim prep (scuff-sand + acetone wipe) are extrapolated from general PVC prep guidance. No direct doctrine production rate for PVC trim exists.
uncertainties.recommendation: Flag PVC prep rates for field calibration. Use conservative estimate (60-80 LF/hr) until calibrated.

uncertainties.detail: Doctrine notes sills 'often receive a distinct high-durability coating' but does not specify whether this means an additional coat or a different product. Current spec assumes same coat system as other trim with production rate penalty for horizontal exposure.
uncertainties.recommendation: Flag for field review. May need sill-specific coating product in materials.json and possible 3rd coat task.

uncertainties.detail: A single house may have fascia at 13ft, window casings at ground level, and corner boards spanning both. The per-component height modifier assignment requires PaintScope to capture height per trim component or per elevation.
uncertainties.recommendation: Engine should support per-item height modifier assignment. Default: fascia/rake/frieze inherit elevation height; casings/sills inherit the floor they serve; corner boards use the predominant height zone.

research_corrections.original_claim: Trim spec should use the same general access_type modifiers (ground/ladder/scaffold/lift) as siding specs
research_corrections.corrected_to: Trim spec uses its own height modifiers from Exterior_Trim_Systems_Doctrine (8ft=1.30, 13ft=1.60, 17ft=1.90, 19ft=2.20). These are more granular and aggressive than general access modifiers because trim requires fine brush detail at height.

research_corrections.original_claim: Window/door glass masking during casing painting should be delegated to window/door specs like siding does
research_corrections.corrected_to: Glass masking IS this spec's responsibility when painting casings. The casing-to-glass edge is a direct cut-in that this spec must own. This is different from siding where glass protection is delegated.

research_corrections.original_claim: Caulk trim-to-siding joints BEFORE primer application
research_corrections.corrected_to: Caulk is applied AFTER primer, not before. Caulk adheres better to primed surfaces than bare substrates. Priming first seals and stabilizes the wood/PVC/composite edges before caulk is applied. Correct sequence: prep → prime → caulk (on primed surfaces) → finish coats.

research_corrections.original_claim: Semi-gloss is the default sheen for exterior trim
research_corrections.corrected_to: There is no locked-in default sheen for exterior trim. Sheen is a project-level selection. The spec must not hardcode a sheen default. If anything, satin is the most common selection in practice, but no default should be imposed.

research_corrections.original_claim: Material waste factor for trim is +15% (MOD_TRIM_WASTE)
research_corrections.corrected_to: Material waste is handled per product at the general level, not per substrate or per spec. Removed MOD_TRIM_WASTE from modifier catalog and findings.

research_corrections.original_claim: Butt joints preferred over miter joints for exterior casings (RF-017)
research_corrections.corrected_to: Removed. This is a carpentry finding, not a painting finding. Joint type is not within the painting spec's scope.

research_corrections.original_claim: Exterior trim is a fine-finish surface
research_corrections.corrected_to: Exterior trim is NOT fine-finish work like interior millwork. It is standard exterior grade work — the same grade as siding in most cases. The visible architectural role justifies QT3 minimum but does not elevate it to fine-finish status.

research_corrections.original_claim: Trim-to-siding caulking is solely this spec's responsibility
research_corrections.corrected_to: Trim-to-siding joint caulking may also be scoped under the siding spec. The estimation engine must deduplicate at project assembly to prevent double-counting caulk labor at the trim-siding junction.
